title: HC and SC – individual balance sheets 31 December N2
text: On 31 December N, HC acquired 100% of the shares of SC for 900 in cash. At that date the book value of SC's net assets (equity) was 350 (capital only). SC had developed a brand internally; its fair value at the acquisition date was estimated at 420. SC's result for N1 was nil.
On 31 December N2 the brand is impaired: its value is now 330. Assume the whole impairment arises in N2 and that there are no intercompany transactions.

title: Corvin plc – retail park measured at cost
text: On 1 January N1 Corvin plc acquired a retail park for €480 million, which it rents out to shops. Corvin measures the park with the cost model and depreciates it straight-line over 40 years (residual value zero).
On 31 December N6, after the depreciation of N6, the CFO notices that prices of retail properties have dropped sharply. Information available on 31 December N6:
– Estimated selling price of the park (net of costs to sell): €300 million.
– Annual rent received: €36 million, paid each year on 31 December, for the remaining 34 years of use.
– Discount rate: 9%. Residual value at the end of the useful life: zero.
Annuity factors at 9%: 30 years 10.27 · 34 years 10.52 · 35 years 10.57 · 40 years 10.76.

title: Marlow SA – lease or bank loan?
text: Marlow SA needs new production equipment with a useful life of 7 years. Marlow already carries a high level of financial debt, and its loan covenants limit net debt to 3 × EBITDA. Instead of borrowing from its bank to buy the equipment, the CFO plans to sign a 6-year lease contract for the equipment, convinced that this will keep financial debt unchanged. Marlow prepares IFRS financial statements.

title: Avarin SA – convertible bond
text: On 1 January N Avarin SA issued a convertible bond with a nominal value of €150 million at par. It carries a coupon of 4%, paid at the end of each year, and is redeemed at par on 31 December N+3 unless converted. Holders may convert at any time into 8 ordinary shares per €100 of bonds.
A conventional bond without the conversion option would have required an interest rate of 6%.
Factors at 6%: annuity factor over 4 years 3.4651; discount factor for year 4 0.7921.
